entries.en: The Buenos Aires Obelisk stands in Plaza de la República at the intersection of 9 de Julio Avenue and Corrientes Street. Built in 1936 to mark the 400th anniversary of the city's first founding, the monument rises 67.5 metres. Today it is a central stop on city walks, with views of the broad avenues of Argentina's capital.

At around 3300 metres, Confluencia is an important early stop on the approach to Aconcagua through the Horcones Valley. On Ada Tours' current expedition, climbers spend the night here before an acclimatisation walk to Plaza Francia and the move to Plaza de Mulas base camp. Explore the route through Confluencia, how the first days work and why this ascent differs from an ordinary walk in the provincial park.

Plaza Dorrego in historic San Telmo features on sightseeing routes through Buenos Aires. Historic façades, cafés and antique shops surround the square, which hosts a famous Sunday market. Ada Tours visits this stop on trips of different lengths, from festive itineraries through 3 countries to an extensive journey across Argentina and Patagonia. Compare the programmes and choose the right one.

Our Chile and Argentina VIP tour offers an optional ten-minute helicopter flight above Ushuaia. Find out where it fits within the 26-day itinerary, what limits apply to a short flight and what must be confirmed before adding it to your programme.

Crooked Tree Wildlife Sanctuary in northern Belize is known for its lagoons and wetland birds. Ada Tours' current itinerary visits it on day 2 before continuing to the Maya ruins of Altun Ha. Explore the actual programme, included services, birdwatching seasonality and how this route differs from visits to other natural areas.

Rio On Pools in western Belize is a series of freshwater cascades among granite rocks in the Mountain Pine Ridge reserve. Two Ada Tours itineraries visit after the ancient Maya city of Caracol and Rio Frio Cave. One lasts 11 days and continues to the Placencia coast; the other covers 8 Central American countries over 26 days. Compare their pace and time for relaxation.

Eduardo Avaroa Reserve in southwestern Bolivia is known for the red waters of Laguna Colorada, green waters near Licancabur Volcano, flamingos and geothermal fields. Travel is by 4x4 because the sights are remote and the roads cross the cold, high-altitude Altiplano. Ada Tours offers a short 3-day jeep trip through the lagoons as well as longer journeys taking in Uyuni, La Paz, Lake Titicaca, Peru or Chile. Compare the stops included in each programme, departure points and time needed in the region.

Tours visiting Bonito in Brazil suit travellers drawn to clear rivers, underground lakes, waterfalls and the nature trails of Mato Grosso do Sul. Some itineraries spend several days in Bonito and the Pantanal, while others include it in a wider journey through Rio de Janeiro, Iguazu Falls and Lençóis Maranhenses. Compare how long each tour spends here, which water excursions it includes and its logistics: a 6-day trip and a 17-day journey offer different experiences.

Jardim da Amazônia Lodge features in an 8-day Ada Tours nature itinerary. Travellers spend the first 2 nights on the southern edge of the Amazon in Mato Grosso, exploring the forest, canoeing on the Claro River and visiting Anaconda Lake. The journey then continues through Bom Jardim, Chapada dos Guimarães and the Northern Pantanal. Discover who this route suits, how much time is spent at the lodge and which arrangements are confirmed in the programme.

A jeep tour of Rocinha in Rio de Janeiro introduces the daily life of a large urban neighbourhood, its street markets and crafts market. We offer 2 formats: a shared group tour with an English-speaking guide for $90 per person, and a private visit with a Russian-speaking guide, for 2 or more participants, from $170 per person.

This 4-hour Ada Tours excursion combines the ascent through Urca to Sugarloaf Mountain with a visit to Rio's historic centre. First admire the city from above, then see historic churches and the cathedral. Learn about both stages of the cable car and the stops included in the route.

This itinerary combines one night in Manaus with 2 nights at Evolution Eco Lodge on the Rio Negro. Over 4 days, planned experiences include the Meeting of the Waters of the Rio Negro and Solimões, encounters with pink river dolphins, a jungle walk, Acajatuba village and a night excursion to look for caimans. Explore transfers, accommodation, included services and how this trip differs from a river cruise or a short VIP tour.

This twelve-day tour combines the samba school parade in Rio, visits to Iguazu Falls on both sides of the border and beach time in Búzios. See how the nights are allocated, how the Brazilian and Argentine sides differ, which Carnival tickets are included and what to budget for flights.

Celebrate New Year on Copacabana and visit both sides of Iguazu Falls in 7 days. The programme includes Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain, a flight to the falls and excursions in Brazil and Argentina, without a further beach stay.

Excursions to Lake Sarmiento on Chile itineraries take in Torres del Paine, viewpoints and Grey Glacier. Choose between a 7-day programme, a VIP itinerary and a journey that also includes Easter Island.

The Guayabero River near La Macarena forms part of routes to the colourful Caño Cristales river. Travellers cover part of the journey by boat before switching to a 4x4 or following a trail on foot. Ada Tours offers 6- and 8-day programmes with this river section. They differ mainly in how deeply they explore the natural area and how many days are reserved for walks.

Mutanzhi is an Indigenous community in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta mountains, along trekking routes to the Lost City. Ada Tours programmes include a visit to the community on one of the trekking days, rather than as a short standalone excursion from Santa Marta. Compare the 7- and 15-day tours to see when you reach Mutanzhi, the walk involved and how to prepare for a respectful visit.

Canopy activities in Monteverde feature in a 26-day journey across eight Central American countries. They take place in the second half of the nineteenth day, after a walk through the cloud forest reserve. The operator, course and participation conditions are confirmed at booking.

A walk through Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve is part of a 26-day journey across eight Central American countries. On the morning of the nineteenth day, you explore the humid montane forest, followed by canopy activities in the afternoon. A quetzal sighting is possible but not guaranteed.

On a twelve-day VIP journey through Costa Rica and Nicaragua, you can replace part of the day around Arenal with an excursion to Monteverde Cloud Forest and Viento Fresco Waterfalls. This is an alternative that changes the day's programme, not an additional guaranteed stop.
A six-hour excursion from Santa Cruz to South Plaza Island: around an hour and a half aboard a yacht, a walk among sea lions and land iguanas, red-and-green vegetation and birdwatching.

Post Office Bay on Floreana Island is known for its old postal barrel, where travellers leave postcards. Our itineraries visit the bay on cruises, including an eight-day voyage aboard Aqua Mare and an eighteen-day Ecuador tour featuring a four-day cruise aboard M/Y Grand Majestic.

The Quijos River features in 2 of our active Ecuador itineraries. Both include approximately 16 km of rafting through grade IV to IV+ rapids on day 9, with a safety briefing and support. They differ in what follows: 13 days on the mainland, or 17 days including an extension to the Galápagos Islands.

Two different Ada Tours itineraries pass through Tena: an active journey with rafting on the Jatunyacu River and a combined trip from the Andes to a lodge on the Napo River, continuing to the Galápagos Islands. When choosing between them, the activities included in the Amazon section matter more than the shared city name.

Yaxha can be added to a Guatemala and Belize trip during a free day after arrival in Petén. The main twelve-day Ada Tours itinerary already includes Tikal the following day. An optional visit to Yaxha offers a second Maya city, but needs to fit around the flight, transfer and rest before the onward journey.

Ada Tours' cultural itineraries including Honduras centre on Copán, the ancient Maya city near the Guatemalan border. Visitors explore carved stelae, the Hieroglyphic Stairway, the acropolis and the history of its Classic-period rulers. Our itineraries connect Copán with Antigua, Tikal, Quiriguá and other Central American heritage sites. Some allow almost a full day at Copán; others include it in a longer journey across 5 to 8 countries. Compare the actual stops, route differences and time available for archaeology.

The 8-day Colombia itinerary 'Season of Colours' includes a dawn canoe outing on the Guayabero River specifically for birdwatching. With luck, pink river dolphins may also appear. The journey includes Chicaque and Caño Cristales, but this dedicated wildlife outing distinguishes it from routes focused on palm valleys, waterfalls and the coast. Compare the included activities with the scenic alternatives.

On the 9- and 14-day tours including Guyana, the included wildlife encounters take place in Suriname: evening outings to look for caimans, and, on the longer itinerary, excursions to observe wildlife around Kabalebo. Guyana itself features Georgetown and a short excursion to Kaieteur Falls. Compare the two routes alongside a separate 7-day scenic alternative.

On current tours that include Mexico, dedicated wildlife encounters take place in Belize and Costa Rica. 'Cancún and Belize' features Hol Chan, with nurse sharks and a sea outing among rays and turtles. The 26-day Central America programme includes a dawn boat trip through Tortuguero. Mexico's cenotes, canyons and forests around Maya sites offer a different, landscape-focused experience.

An excursion to a Yucatán cenote and the pyramids of Chichén Itzá ends with a transfer to Cancún. It takes place on day 5 of Ada Tours' 26-day journey through Central America. See how the day is arranged, why the exact cenote name still needs confirmation and why a stop in Cancún differs from an extended beach stay.

Ik Kil Cenote on the Yucatán Peninsula is often visited on the same day as Chichén Itzá. It appears in 2 Ada Tours journeys: an activity-packed 6-day trip to Mexico's archaeological sites and an 11-day tour travelling through Cancún into Belize. Choose according to whether you want more ancient cities or a combination of Maya heritage, the Caribbean Sea and a second country.

Monte Albán, the ancient Zapotec ceremonial centre overlooking the Oaxaca Valley, features in 2 active Ada Tours itineraries: a short 5-day visit to Oaxaca and a 12-day journey across Mexico. On the shorter trip, all 4 nights are spent in Oaxaca and the archaeological visit is combined with craft villages. On the longer itinerary, Monte Albán is visited on day 7 between Mexico City and Yucatán. Compare travel time, excursions, included services and what to expect when exploring the ruins.

Puebla features in 2 itineraries with different aims: a 9-day Day of the Dead journey and a 7-day pilgrimage through central Mexico. The first includes 2 nights in Puebla and festive traditions in neighbouring towns. The second visits the city on a sightseeing day from Mexico City, along with the shrines of Tlaxcala and Ocotlán. Compare the programme, dates, overnight stays and what the excursions actually include.

This 6-day journey connects Mexico City's historic centre and Teotihuacán with ancient Maya cities on the Yucatán Peninsula. A domestic flight from Mexico City to Mérida is followed by visits to Uxmal, Kabah and Chichén Itzá. The domestic flight ticket is paid for separately. To keep the day 4 excursion, you need to arrive in Mérida before 13:00.

The expedition cruise from Argentina to Antarctica in our current itinerary begins in Ushuaia. Over 6 days the ship crosses the Beagle Channel, passes Chile's Cape Horn and the Drake Passage, and reaches the South Shetland Islands. The return from King George Island is by air to Punta Arenas. This combination of sea passage and a one-way flight is an important part of choosing an Antarctic expedition.

The sea portion of the 'Antarctica Express' expedition runs from Ushuaia via Cape Horn and the Drake Passage to the South Shetland Islands. Chile features both at the start, via Puerto Williams, and at the end, when travellers fly from King George Island to Punta Arenas. Explore what the 6-day expedition includes, when landings may be possible and why the return flight requires some schedule flexibility.

Argentina, Bolivia and Brazil feature together on extended South American itineraries covering Rio de Janeiro, both sides of Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires and the Uyuni Salt Flat. Every current programme with this combination also includes Chile and Peru. Compare all 5 countries, the order of flights, the high-altitude stretch through the Atacama Desert, acclimatisation in Bolivia, visa requirements, seasons and additional costs.

Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Peru make it possible to combine Iguazu Falls, high-altitude Andean lagoons, the Uyuni Salt Flat, Lake Titicaca and Machu Picchu in one journey. The 4 selected countries are part of the main itineraries, but the current programmes also visit Chile. Travel to Bolivia is arranged via Santiago and the Atacama Desert. Compare the length of the mountain section, border crossings, Machu Picchu reservations and documents required for all 5 countries.

Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Bolivia bring together Rio's Atlantic coast, Iguazu Falls, the capitals of the Río de la Plata region and the high-altitude Uyuni Salt Flat. Our programmes pass through Chile and then continue across Peru; the longer version also visits Ecuador and Colombia. When choosing, account for the return to Argentina after Montevideo, different currencies, flights via Santiago, off-road travel in Bolivia and major changes in altitude and temperature.

The main adventure section of our itineraries combining Argentina, Bolivia and Chile runs by 4x4 from San Pedro de Atacama to Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat. Argentina contributes walks near Iguazu Falls and a visit to Buenos Aires, rather than a separate mountain trek. These countries form part of journeys through 5, 6 or 8 countries, so the sequence of transfers, altitudes above 4000 metres and the actual level of physical exertion matter.

On this journey through Argentina, Bolivia and Chile, the expedition cruise begins only after the high-altitude jeep itinerary and Patagonia. Travellers first cross Bolivia's Altiplano, then board a ship in Punta Arenas, sail through the fjords and Beagle Channel towards Cape Horn, and disembark in Ushuaia. When choosing the trip, distinguish the overland expedition, marine landings and onward flights through Argentina.

Argentina's Iguazu Falls, the Atacama Desert, a two-day jeep journey through Bolivia and marine excursions in the Galápagos Islands are combined in one trip. Compare the types of activity, high-altitude requirements, crossings through other countries and alternative island routes.

The adventure element of a journey through Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia is centred on Bolivia's Altiplano: 2 days by 4x4 across lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat. Argentina offers walks at Iguazu Falls, while Colombia adds an excursion to El Peñón and Guatapé. In our programme, these countries are part of a 32-day itinerary through 8 nations, which matters when judging physical demands, connections and recovery time.

The most intensive adventure section of this selection crosses Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons by jeep. In Ecuador the journey continues to the Galápagos Islands, in Argentina it includes walks near Iguazu Falls, and Colombia adds the mountain landscapes of Guatapé. These are parts of a longer journey through 8 countries, not a standalone four-country expedition.

On our eight-country journey, the adventure activities in this four-country selection are mainly in Bolivia and the Galápagos Islands. In Bolivia, travellers cross high-altitude lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat by 4x4. Ecuador includes a marine excursion and island walks, while Peru brings Andean transfers and a visit to Machu Picchu. Argentina adds Iguazu Falls; technical trekking and mountaineering are not part of the programme.

On itineraries covering Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru, the adventure begins at Iguazu Falls, continues through the dry landscapes of the Atacama Desert and reaches the high roads of the Andes and Machu Picchu. However, the longest off-road section of the eligible journeys is in Bolivia, the fifth main country on these tours. Compare the days spent walking, flying and travelling by jeep to choose according to the actual physical demands.

Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Uruguay all feature in Ada Tours' extensive 32-day programme through 8 countries. Argentina and Uruguay come together: Buenos Aires is followed by a day trip by ferry to Montevideo. Santiago and the Atacama Desert come next, and the Colombian cities close the journey after the sections through Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. This selection helps compare the wider geography; it is not a standalone four-country tour.

Argentina, Chile and Peru bring together Buenos Aires, Santiago and the Inca heritage of Cusco. In our current selection, these countries form part of journeys through 4 or 5 nations, rather than a ready-made trip visiting exactly three. When choosing, consider the additional stops in Brazil and Bolivia, flights, time reserved for Machu Picchu and the climatic contrast between summer in Buenos Aires and the rainy season in the Peruvian Andes.

Argentina and Colombia offer two very different natural experiences on one extended journey: the humid forests and Iguazu Falls on the Argentine section, followed by Antioquia's mountains, El Peñón rock and the Guatapé reservoir in Colombia. The current Ada Tours itinerary also visits 6 other countries, so weeks of travel separate these landscapes. Choose with both the sights and the pace of the journey in mind.

In one extended Ada Tours itinerary, Argentina and Ecuador reveal 2 distinct cultural worlds of South America. In Buenos Aires, travellers explore immigrant neighbourhoods and tango; in Quito, the colonial centre, architecture of the Quito School and the history of the equator. Between them, the route crosses Chile, Bolivia and Peru, visiting pre-Inca and Inca heritage sites. This is a cultural journey through eight countries, not a short flight between two capitals.

In our current 32-day journey through 8 South American countries, Argentina, Ecuador and Peru offer three different natural experiences: the rainforest and Iguazu Falls, the protected wildlife of the Galápagos Islands and high-altitude Lake Titicaca. This is not a direct three-country itinerary, as there are other stops between the selected countries. Compare the programme, visiting rules and contrasting ecosystems.

The adventure selection for Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay forms part of an extensive route through 8 South American countries. Argentina includes walks by Iguazu Falls, Ecuador features Quito and a marine excursion in the Galápagos Islands, while Uruguay is visited on a day trip to Montevideo. The most demanding high-altitude jeep sections take place in Bolivia. See which activities require physical preparation and how walks, island excursions and the off-road expedition differ.

Belize, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Costa Rica make an appealing combination of Maya heritage, colonial cities, volcanic landscapes and tropical forests. On our 'Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days' tour, all four are part of the main route, but Honduras and El Salvador lie between Guatemala and Nicaragua. Check the order of stops, flights, CA-4 entry arrangements and the differences in weather between Guatemala's highlands and Costa Rica's waterways.

On adventure itineraries combining Brazil and Bolivia, Rio de Janeiro and Iguazu Falls come first. After Argentina and Chile, the expedition section begins with 4x4 travel across the Altiplano, lagoons and Uyuni. Allow for major changes in altitude, temperature and pace; this two-country selection is not a direct transfer between Brazil and Bolivia.

Natural experiences differ dramatically between journeys through Bolivia and Brazil: the humid Atlantic Forest and Iguazu Falls give way to high-altitude lagoons, salt flats and the dry Andean air. In our current programmes, these are parts of larger routes through 5 to 8 countries, not a standalone two-country wildlife safari. Explore the included natural stops and how to prepare for changes in climate and altitude.

This four-country combination brings together Brazil's Iguazu Falls, Chile's Atacama Desert, Bolivia's lagoons and Uyuni Salt Flat, and then Quito and Ecuador's Galápagos Islands. On Ada Tours' 32-day itinerary, the landscape changes from humid tropics to elevations above 4000 metres and island coasts. The programme crosses Peru between Bolivia and Ecuador, so the altitude sequence, flights to the Galápagos and island conservation rules are particularly important.

The adventure in combining Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador lies in changing travel styles: walks at Iguazu Falls and in Rio, a two-day jeep route through Bolivia's highlands and marine excursions in the Galápagos Islands. On the current 32-day itinerary through eight countries, the Bolivian section demands particular attention to altitude, while the Galápagos programme offers a choice between two island routes.

On Ada Tours' 32-day journey, the history of Bolivia, Chile, Colombia and Ecuador is explored through Tiwanaku and La Paz, Santiago's neighbourhoods, colonial Quito, Cartagena and Bogotá's museums. These are stops on a route through 8 countries, not a separate four-country itinerary. Compare the actual heritage sites included and why other countries and natural excursions lie between them.

Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador form a consecutive Andean section of a longer Ada Tours journey: San Pedro de Atacama, the Altiplano lagoons and Uyuni, Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu, then Quito and the Galápagos Islands. In the current 32-day route through eight countries, these destinations follow one another, but transfers involve flights, 4x4 vehicles, border crossings and buses. Altitude, archaeological site access and island conservation rules all matter when choosing the trip.

Bolivia, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay feature in an extensive Ada Tours journey through 8 South American countries. The main adventure section is 2 high-altitude days by 4x4 in Bolivia; Peru adds travel through the Andes and Machu Picchu, Colombia adds El Peñón and Guatapé, and Uruguay a city stop in Montevideo. This is not a standalone tour limited to these four countries, so compare the full sequence of flights and the physical demands of the 32-day itinerary.
